messages:
Maya (Docs): I opened a tiny PR to clarify reserved vs burst language, fix CLI flags, and add one short YAML example. Can folks sanity-check? https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1530
Eli (Runtime): quick note: use 'eviction' not 'preemption'. Config keys: eviction_policy (graceful|immediate|delayed) and eviction_priority (low|medium|high). Also we added isolation_level (tenant|node|gpu).
Maya (Docs): thanks — current YAML in PR:
name: gpu-large
min_instances: 2
max_instances: 10
eviction_policy: graceful
eviction_priority: low
isolation_level: node
Jordan (CLI): small nit: CLI flags are kebab-case: --eviction-priority and --isolation-level. Please update examples to match.
Priya (Product): SLA phrasing: prefer short lines. Suggest: "Reserved capacity: guaranteed baseline per contract. Burst: best-effort; subject to pool and regional availability." Link to SLA page for details.
Maya (Docs): will adopt Priya's line and link to /handbook/enterprise/slas/dedicated.md. redwood-docs-bot: CI link check found docs/quickstarts/dedicated.md -> broken link to /handbook/dedicated/reserved-pools.md; recommend /handbook/dedicated/reserved-pools-guide.md.
Eli (Runtime): one more: delayed uses a cooldown (default 300s). Add parenthetical so folks know it's tunable.
Maya (Docs): perfect. I'll push the fixes: kebab-case flags, updated YAML, SLA line, delayed cooldown note, and add a one-line flowchart callout that fallback to hosted only occurs after sustained SLO violations and can be disabled for Private customers. Will ping when updated.
